To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the FINmaj mutation in the titin protein causes the TMD disease and that calpain 3 plays a major role in the pathogenesis.
the FINmaj mutation leads to the secondary loss of calpain 2 and 3, which in turn leads to the myopathology observed in TMD patients.

1) we generated a mouse carrying the FINmaj founder mutation and that this mouse develops a muscular dystrophy phenotype; 2) we showed that the FINmaj mutation leads to the secondary loss of calpain 4, a protease partner of titin, which explains the myopathy; 3) we showed that this myopathy is reversed by the removal of calpain 5, demonstrating the participation of calpain in this disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new mouse model that reproduces the TMD and LGM2J phenotypes.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for muscular dystrophies.
the study of the molecular mechanisms underlying muscle degeneration.

the FINmaj mutation in titin causes a severe myopathy and heart failure, and that the secondary deficiency of calpaing 3 is the main cause of muscle pathology.
the FINmaj mutation in titin leads to a secondary deficiency in calpain 3 that results in a myopathy that can be corrected by the re-introduction of calpain 2 in the mouse model.
FINmaj is a dominant-negative titinopathy with a secondary deficiency in calpain 3.
